newsitem.title: USA: Wash. state bacterial outbreak linked to juice.
newsitem.headline: Wash. state bacterial outbreak linked to juice.

text.p: An outbreak of the baterial disease E. coli that has sickened at least 13 children and young adults over the past two weeks have been traced to tainted juice, Washington state officials said Wednesday.
Matt Ashworth, spokesman for the state Department of Health, said 10 confirmed cases of the disease have been conclusively tied to Odwalla Inc. fruit juice.

Ashworth did not have immediate details, but a news conference was scheduled to discuss the findings. An executive of Odwalla, based in Half Moon Bay, Calif., had not heard about the outbreak and had no immediate comment.
Since last week 13 people in western Washington, ranging in age from 2 to their early 20s, have been sickened by the bateria, and another four cases were suspected but not confirmed, Ashworth said.
Several children have required hospitalization and kidney dialysis and at least one 2-year-old boy remained hospitalized in satisfactory condition.
It was the state's worst outbreak of the disease since 1993, when more than 400 people were sickened and several children died after eating tainted hamburger meat at Jack-in-the-Box restaurants.
